record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.context_brief: Quaternionic scattering matrices as boundary values
record.original_question: In quaternionic quantum mechanics, prove or disprove that the elements of the quaternionic scattering matrix are boundary values of regular quaternionic functions, in the sense of the quaternionic hyperfunctions introduced by the authors. The obstruction is that physicists use a formal analogue of exp(z) to build scattering matrices, but that exponential is not regular in the Cauchy-Fueter sense.

evidence.quote: Problem: It is possible to prove that the elements of the quaternionic scattering matrix are boundary values of regular functions?
the non-regularity of the exponential function used in this case is an obstruction to restore the theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A quaternion-valued function f of a quaternionic variable q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k is called (left) Cauchy–Fueter regular on an open set U ⊂ H if it is C^1 and satisfies the Cauchy–Fueter equation
    (∂/∂x_0 + i ∂/∂x_1 + j ∂/∂x_2 + k ∂/∂x_3) f = 0   on U.
Building on this notion, one can develop a theory of quaternionic hyperfunctions: a hyperfunction on a real domain Ω ⊂ R^n (n ≤ 4) embedded in H is represented as an equivalence class of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions defined on a complex/quaternionic neighborhood minus Ω, modulo regular functions on the full neighborhood, so that every such hyperfunction admits an interpretation as a boundary value of a regular quaternionic function.

In quaternionic quantum mechanics, observable quantities (in particular the entries of the scattering matrix S) are quaternion-valued, and physicists construct S via a formal series analogue of the complex exponential exp(z) = Σ z^n / n!, applied to a quaternionic "Hamiltonian" expression. The resulting formal quaternionic exponential is not, in general, a Cauchy–Fueter regular function of its quaternionic argument.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following: every entry of the quaternionic scattering matrix in quaternionic quantum mechanics can be realized as the boundary value of a Cauchy–Fueter regular quaternionic function in the sense of quaternionic hyperfunctions. In particular, decide whether the non-regularity of the formal quaternionic exponential used to construct S is a genuine obstruction or can be circumvented by an alternative regular representation.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific published resolution was located for the question of representing entries of the quaternionic scattering matrix as boundary values of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions via quaternionic hyperfunctions. The status appears unresolved in the accessible literature.
